title: Reference program: standardize HubSpot CRM fields + lightweight automation (readiness, approvals, reminders)
creator: Isabelle Laurent
body:
Context
We’re launching the structured case study + customer reference program and need a single, consistent source of truth in HubSpot for:
- who is eligible/ready to be a reference
- what approvals are in place (logo/quote/public case study vs reference-call-only)
- who owns next steps (AE/CSM/Marketing)
- lightweight reminders/alerts so requests don’t stall

This ticket is the Engineering implementation portion (property creation + basic workflow automation). Requirements and routing intent are defined in PM-701 (intake form + routing rules). This ticket assumes we’re not building a new app; we’re using HubSpot native properties + workflows + Slack/email notifications.

Goals
1) Standardize CRM properties so Sales/CS/Marketing are using the same fields and definitions.
2) Add minimal automation to reduce manual follow-up (stale statuses, missing approvals, scheduling SLA nudges).
3) Make reporting possible for program KPIs: # ready references, time-to-ready, # reference calls completed (tracked separately), and case study approval stages.

Non-goals
- No custom UI or private app build.
- No complex lead scoring.
- No changes to sales pipeline stages (this is reference-program-specific metadata).

Proposed HubSpot data model
Object scope: Company properties (primary), Contact properties (spokesperson/champion metadata), and Deal properties (optional; only where reference readiness differs by product line).

A) Company properties (new unless noted)
1) Reference program status (dropdown)
   - Not a candidate
   - Candidate (identified)
   - Outreach in progress
   - Interested (verbal)
   - Enrolled (kickoff complete)
   - Ready for reference calls
   - On hold (customer bandwidth)
   - Retired (no longer eligible)

2) Reference readiness (dropdown)
   - Not assessed
   - Needs proof points (metrics not validated)
   - Needs champion confirmation
   - Needs legal approval
   - Ready (approved + briefed)

3) Reference participation type (multi-select)
   - Reference call (private)
   - Public case study (web/PDF)
   - Quote only
   - Logo only
   - Partner co-marketing (marketplace)

4) Approval status: logo (dropdown)
   - Not requested
   - Requested
   - Approved
   - Declined

5) Approval status: quotes (dropdown)
   - Not requested
   - Requested
   - Approved
   - Declined

6) Approval status: public case study (dropdown)
   - Not requested
   - Requested
   - In review (customer)
   - Approved
   - Declined

7) Reference call boundaries (free text)
   Guidance for AEs/SEs: topics to avoid, what can/can’t be shared, any required disclaimers.

8) Reference call cadence allowed (dropdown)
   - Ad hoc
   - 1 per month
   - 1 per quarter
   - Other (see notes)

9) Reference program owner (HubSpot owner field)
   Default to CSM owner; fallback to AE owner when no CSM.

10) Last reference request date (date)
11) Last reference call completed date (date)
12) Reference program notes (long text)

B) Contact properties
1) Reference spokesperson (boolean)
2) Spokesperson role (dropdown)
   - Engineering
   - Product
   - Security/Compliance
   - Executive

3) Reference call availability window (free text)

C) Audit/reporting helper properties
1) Reference program SLA status (dropdown)
   - On track
   - Needs follow-up (7d)
   - Escalate (14d)

2) Approval packet link (URL)
   Link to Google Drive folder containing release form + approval emails.

Automation (HubSpot workflows)
1) Stale status reminder (company)
Trigger:
- Reference program status in [Outreach in progress, Interested (verbal), Enrolled (kickoff complete)] AND
- updated more than 14 days ago
Actions:
- Send internal email to Reference program owner
- Optional Slack notification to #customer-success (confirm with Rachel Kim)

2) Ready gatekeeper check (company)
Trigger:
- Reference program status set to “Ready for reference calls”
If any of the following are missing:
- Reference participation type does not include “Reference call (private)” OR
- Reference call boundaries is empty OR
- At least one contact flagged as Reference spokesperson = true is missing
Then:
- Set Reference readiness to “Needs champion confirmation”
- Create task for owner: “Confirm spokesperson + boundaries before accepting requests”

3) Approval tracking nudges (company)
Trigger:
- Reference participation type contains “Public case study (web/PDF)” AND
- Approval status: public case study is “Requested” for 10+ days
Actions:
- Create task for Marketing owner (Camila Reyes / Soojin Lee depending on routing) OR company owner if no marketing owner
- Email reminder with link to Approval packet link property

4) Optional: reference request intake integration (blocked on PM-701)
Once PM-701 intake form exists and creates a ticket/task:
- Auto-post to Slack channel #sales-enablement or route to AE/CSM
- Auto-set Reference program status to “Reference request received” (if we add this status) or create a task

Permissions / governance
- Only Marketing Ops (Tyler Benson) + CRM Ops (Isabelle Laurent) can edit dropdown values.
- Sales/CS can edit current status and notes.
- Legal fields are status-only; do not store contract language or confidential security artifacts directly in HubSpot notes (link out to Drive).

Acceptance criteria
- All properties listed above exist in HubSpot with the exact internal names and dropdown values documented below.
- A single “Reference Program” property group is created so fields are easy to find.
- Workflows 1–3 are active in production and tested with 2 sample company records.
- Reporting sanity check: Isabelle can build a simple saved view: (Reference readiness = Ready) + (Participation type contains Reference call) and it returns expected companies.
- Field definitions are documented in Confluence/enablement page (link added here once published).

Internal property naming (draft; confirm with Isabelle before creation)
- ref_program_status
- ref_readiness
- ref_participation_type
- ref_approval_logo
- ref_approval_quotes
- ref_approval_public_case_study
- ref_call_boundaries
- ref_call_cadence
- ref_owner
- ref_last_request_date
- ref_last_call_completed_date
- ref_program_notes
- ref_sla_status
- ref_approval_packet_link
- contact_ref_spokesperson
- contact_ref_spokesperson_role
- contact_ref_availability_window

Rollout plan
- Phase 1 (this ticket): create properties + workflows in sandbox, validate, then deploy to prod.
- Phase 2: backfill 5–10 known candidates (Arcadia Health, QuantaPay, NovaDocs, HelioSupport, VectorForge) with owners in a working session.
- Phase 3: add to internal enablement doc + announce in #announcements with “how to request a reference”.

Risks / gotchas
- HubSpot multi-select fields can be awkward in workflows; keep logic simple.
- Avoid creating automation that spams Slack—start with email/task creation, then add Slack if needed.
- Ensure we don’t represent “Ready” as a legal approval; approvals are separate fields.

Open questions
1) Do we want “Reference request received” as an explicit status, or keep requests tracked via tasks only?
2) Who is the default owner when AE and CSM differ (or when CSM is unassigned)? Proposal: ref_owner defaults to CSM owner; if none, AE owner.
3) Should “Last reference call completed date” be automated via meeting outcome logging, or manually updated for now?

Progress updates
- 2025-06-05 (Logan): Drafted property list + workflow logic; waiting on Isabelle to confirm dropdown values and internal names.
- 2025-06-12 (Isabelle): Confirmed we should keep approvals separate (logo/quote/case study). Requested an ‘Approval packet link’ URL property.
- 2025-06-18 (Logan): Built workflows #1 and #3 in sandbox; testing edge cases with multi-select participation type. Next: create property group + deploy to prod after review.
